actions.reason: ‘AcquisitionStrategy’ in active learning usually denotes the same core concept as the active learning strategy/method itself. At this granularity it is a naming variant of the general ActiveLearning method class, so it is merged as a synonym.

Represents the process/loop view of active learning rather than a distinct method category. This process notion is not essential for distinguishing methods and can be modeled procedurally if needed, so the class is deprecated to reduce clutter.

In this ontology, ‘ActiveLearningStrategy’ and ‘ActiveLearning’ both stand for the general family of methods under ActiveLearningMethod. The distinction is largely terminological here, so we treat them as the same conceptual class and merge via alias.

Uncertainty-based methods form a core, widely recognized category in active learning taxonomies. This is a critical distinction users will likely query for, so it is kept explicitly as a subclass of the general ActiveLearning class.

Diversity-based selection is another standard family of active learning methods, orthogonal to purely uncertainty-based approaches. This is an important top-level method category and should remain as a dedicated subclass.

Representativeness-based methods strongly overlap with diversity/density notions already captured by DiversityBasedActiveLearning and DensityBasedActiveLearning. To avoid a fine-grained but redundant split, this class is deprecated in favor of those broader categories.
This denotes a taxonomy about representativeness-based methods rather than a method type itself. It is meta-level, unused, and adds little modeling value at this stage, so it is deprecated.

Representation-learning-based active learning is a narrower design pattern, largely subsumed within modern DeepActiveLearning techniques. Given the goal of a compact ontology and the presence of DeepActiveLearning as a broader key class, this extra specialization is deprecated.

Expected model change is a canonical and conceptually distinct active learning criterion class, separate from simple uncertainty sampling. It is important in standard taxonomies and therefore kept as a subclass of ActiveLearning.

Pool-based active learning defines a fundamental operational setting (access to an unlabeled pool) that cuts across many strategies. This scenario distinction is central in the literature and is preserved as a subclass.

Stream-based (online) active learning is another core setting distinct from pool-based approaches. Because this difference is methodologically important, it is retained as a subclass of ActiveLearning.

Batch-mode active learning (querying multiple instances at once) is a standard variant with nontrivial methodological implications. It is kept as a dedicated subclass to capture this widely recognized distinction.

‘Framework’ refers to an architectural or software-level packaging of active learning methods rather than a distinct method type. Since process/architecture distinctions are not modeled elsewhere and this class is unused, it is deprecated for compactness.

Disagreement-based methods (e.g., query-by-committee) form a major family of active learning algorithms distinct from simple uncertainty sampling. This is a key conceptual category and is kept as a subclass of ActiveLearning.

Density-based approaches weight informativeness by data density and are a standard class of methods complementing pure uncertainty criteria. This high-level category is important enough to preserve as a subclass.

Clustering-based methods can be viewed as concrete realizations of density/representativeness-based strategies. To avoid a proliferation of implementation-specific subclasses, this is deprecated in favor of the more general DensityBasedActiveLearning (and Diversity-based) categories.

Random sampling is the standard baseline against which active learning methods are compared. Even though it is not strictly ‘active’, it is conceptually important for evaluation and is kept as a subclass under ActiveLearningMethod via ActiveLearning.

Hybrid strategies combine multiple criteria (e.g., uncertainty + diversity). This can be modeled via properties or multiple classification of individual methods without a dedicated hybrid superclass. To keep the hierarchy lean, this generic hybrid class is deprecated.

Deep active learning is central to the domain of this ontology and represents methods specifically tailored to deep models. This is a core specialization of the general ActiveLearning concept and should remain as a named subclass.

Bayesian active learning is a major methodological paradigm (e.g., BALD, Bayesian experimental design) that cuts across several criteria families. Its prominence in the literature justifies keeping it as an explicit subclass of ActiveLearning.

comment: ActiveLearning is chosen as the canonical, general method class under ActiveLearningMethod. Terminological variants (AcquisitionStrategy, ActiveLearningStrategy) are aliased to it. Process/architecture and overly narrow or overlapping method patterns are deprecated. Core, widely recognized methodological and scenario distinctions (uncertainty-, diversity-, disagreement-, density-based, expected model change, pool/stream/batch settings, deep and Bayesian active learning, and the random baseline) are preserved as subclasses to maintain an informative yet compact taxonomy.

Historically obtained labeled data is still just labeled dataset; temporal provenance can be represented via metadata instead of a distinct class.

actions.reason: SampleSpace is effectively the set of possible data instances, which in this ontology is captured by InputSpace; no competency questions distinguish them, so we collapse to a single input/sample space concept.

DataSpace is used as a generic name for the domain of instances; this overlaps with InputSpace and SampleSpace. With no usage evidence to justify a distinction, treat DataSpace as a synonym of InputSpace.
DataSpaceConcept is just a verbose variant of DataSpace and adds no clear semantic distinction; merge into the canonical InputSpace concept.

FeatureSpace and InputSpace are often used interchangeably in ML/AL to denote the vector space of instances; in the absence of CQs that rely on a separation between raw-input and feature space, we collapse them to a single InputSpace concept.

RepresentationSpace is a near-synonym of FeatureSpace (space of learned representations). Since FeatureSpace is already aliased to InputSpace and there are no usage constraints, RepresentationSpace is also treated as an alias of InputSpace.

InfiniteInputSpace is an unused, overly specific variant of InputSpace (distinguished only by cardinality). This detail is better captured via properties or annotations rather than a separate class, so the class is deprecated.

VersionSpace is the subset of the HypothesisSpace consistent with the observed data. This is a well-established, more specific notion that is important for version-space based active learning strategies, so it is kept as a subclass of HypothesisSpace rather than merged away.

HypothesisSpace denotes the set of candidate models/hypotheses, which is conceptually orthogonal to the instance/input space. This distinction is fundamental in learning theory and active learning (e.g., version-space methods), so HypothesisSpace is kept distinct from InputSpace and other data spaces.

LabelSpace denotes the set of possible labels/outputs, which is orthogonal to the instance/input space and the hypothesis space. Many active learning strategies depend on properties of the label space (e.g., binary vs multi-class vs structured outputs), so this concept is kept distinct.

comment: Consolidated multiple loosely differentiated ‘space’ classes into a single canonical InputSpace to minimize redundancy: SampleSpace, DataSpace, DataSpaceConcept, FeatureSpace, and RepresentationSpace are treated as naming variants of the same underlying concept. InfiniteInputSpace is deprecated as an unused, overly specific variant. HypothesisSpace and LabelSpace are retained as distinct because they represent fundamentally different domains (models and labels) that are central to active learning theory. VersionSpace is preserved as a subclass of HypothesisSpace, reflecting its standard role as the data-consistent subset of hypotheses and its importance for version-space based methods.
